meta.title: 古問 LORE
meta.description: Start from a question you care about, read the classic itself, form your own view — then talk.

home.heroBody: LORE starts from questions you face today and takes you to texts written two thousand years ago. AI helps you understand — it never answers for you. Write your own view first; then you see everyone else's.
home.barriersTitle: Why are the classics so hard to read?

why.problem: You don't know why you should read them
why.solution: Start from a contemporary question, not a book title.

understand.solution: AI explains words, people and history — but never gives you a conclusion.

stop.solution: Write your own answer first to unlock others' views and join the discussion.

sections.title: What we collect
sections.body: Your email address (used only to sign you in, never shown publicly), your nickname and language, and what you write on LORE: first thoughts, reflections, replies, likes, reports and feedback. We don't collect your real name, phone number or location.

sections.title: Reading activity
sections.body: To measure things like reading completion, we record when you open a question, open the text, finish reading, ask the AI, submit a reflection and reply. Signed-out visitors are counted only by a random ID stored in the browser, which is not linked to anyone's identity.

sections.title: The AI Companion and AI Insight
sections.body: When you ask the AI Companion something, your question, any passage you selected and the excerpt are sent to Anthropic's Claude API to produce an explanation. We record only how many questions you asked, not the conversation. To generate an AI Insight, the text of submitted reflections (without nicknames or any identifying details) is sent to the same service to be summarised.

sections.title: Who sees your writing
sections.body: A submitted reflection is shown with your nickname to readers who have submitted their own; if you post anonymously, no nickname is shown. Your first thought and drafts are visible only to you. Admins can see all content in order to handle reports.

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
sections.body: We use only the cookies needed to keep you signed in, plus a random visitor ID stored in your browser for statistics. There is no advertising or third-party tracking.

sections.title: Deleting your data
sections.body: On the "Me" page you can delete any reflection, or permanently delete your whole account. Deleting your account also deletes your reflections, replies, likes and feedback; reading records are kept without your identity for overall statistics.

guidelines.title: Community guidelines
guidelines.intro: LORE is a place to read the text first, then talk seriously. Please help keep it that way.

sections.title: Read, then respond
sections.body: Before replying, read the text and the other person's reflection. Respond to ideas, not to people.

sections.title: Respect different views
sections.body: There is no single right answer on LORE. Disagreeing is welcome, but give your reasons. No mockery, abuse or personal attacks.

sections.title: Not allowed
sections.body: Profanity, hate speech or discrimination, harassment, threats, sexual content, advertising or spam, and sharing anyone's private information.

sections.title: Protect privacy
sections.body: Don't include your own or anyone else's real name, contact details or other identifying information in reflections or replies.

sections.title: Respect copyright
sections.body: When quoting the text or other works, quote briefly and give the source. Don't paste long passages of copyrighted translations or articles.

sections.title: Reporting
sections.body: If you see content that breaks these guidelines, press "Report". A moderator will review it and may hide or delete it; accounts with serious or repeated violations may be suspended.
